question.problem: What is ${\int }_{2}^{5}2{x}^{1/3}\,\text{d}x$ expressed as the limit of a left Riemann sum?
question.worked_solution:
The definite integral can be defined in terms of the limit of a left Riemann sum as

$$
{\int }_{a}^{b}f(x)\text{d}x={lim}_{n\to \infty }{\sum }_{j=0}^{n-1}f({x}_{j})\cdot Δx,
$$

    

where $Δx=\frac{b-a}{n}$ and ${x}_{j}=a+jΔx.$

In the definite integral

$$
{\int }_{2}^{5}2{x}^{1/3}\,\text{d}x,
$$

the function is $f(x)=2{x}^{1/3},$ the lower bound is $a=2,$ and the upper bound is $b=5.$ So, we have

$$
Δx=\frac{5-2}{n}=\frac{3}{n},
$$

and therefore

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{2}^{5}2{x}^{1/3}\,\text{d}x & ={lim}_{n\to \infty }{\sum }_{j=0}^{n-1}f({x}_{j})\cdot Δx \\  & ={lim}_{n\to \infty }{\sum }_{j=0}^{n-1}[f(2+j\cdot \frac{3}{n})\cdot \frac{3}{n}] \\  & ={lim}_{n\to \infty }{\sum }_{j=0}^{n-1}[f(2+\frac{3j}{n})\cdot \frac{3}{n}] \\  & ={lim}_{n\to \infty }{\sum }_{j=0}^{n-1}[2{(2+\frac{3j}{n})}^{1/3}\cdot \frac{3}{n}].\end{aligned}
$$
